<reason>The motion explicitly stipulates "even if lenders cut access," putting the burden on PRO to show that tradeoff is worth accepting. CON (A) built its case directly on that clause: caps don't reprice risk downward, they eliminate the loan for the marginal borrower, and the excluded population includes people who would have used the card productively (a repair, a medical bill) alongside those who would stall — a cap cannot sort between them. CON's pressure questions forced PRO to concede that losing the only qualifying card is a genuine access loss and that a cap cannot surgically separate good-use from bad-use borrowers within a risk band. That second concession is especially damaging because it directly contradicts PRO's opening claim that a cap "zeroes out the specific practice of harvesting the most desperate" while sparing reasonable lending — PRO's own rebuttal admits the cap is just as blunt as the status quo. PRO's central empirical claim — that clustering of rates near the legal ceiling proves captivity pricing rather than real cost — was asserted repeatedly but never demonstrated, and CON's "binding constraint, not proof of surplus" response went largely unanswered. PRO's strongest material (the "arithmetic" of compounding, the bridge/swamp metaphor) is rhetorically effective but doesn't resolve which population is actually larger or more representative, whereas CON kept returning concretely to the specific excluded borrower the motion forces PRO to sacrifice. PRO's opening was also clipped for exceeding the word limit, a real execution cost. Overall CON built a tighter, more consistent path that directly engaged the "even if" clause; PRO's case had good rhetorical moments but left a live internal contradiction unresolved.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's pressure questions (Q1/Q2 in Turn 6) forcing PRO to admit both that losing the only qualifying card is a real access loss and that a cap cannot distinguish good-use from bad-use borrowers within a risk band — conceded in [B4.1] and [B4.3] — directly undercut PRO's opening claim that the cap surgically removes only extraction while sparing reasonable lending.</best_rebuttal>
